entity.name: MapSmith
entity.description: Maintainer of MapSmith, an open-source MCP server for professional GIS geoprocessing with verifiable provenance. Work is unfunded to date. As of 2026-09-29: a catalogue of 77 operations, more than 1600 closed-form tests, a 375-run published benchmark, and three repositories archived with DOIs — all built without external support.

projects.name: MapSmith
projects.description: An MCP server for professional GIS geoprocessing — buffers, overlays, reprojections, zonal statistics, terrain and hydrology — where every output carries a provenance manifest: input checksums, exact parameters, motivated CRS decisions, engine versions, and the verification checks that ran. Geometry and numbers always come from engine executions, never from a language model. The aim is that an analysis produced by an agent can be defended afterwards, by someone who was not there when it ran.

channels.description: Written contact for funders. Arrangements are agreed in writing; no payment provider is published here.

plans.name: A correctness suite for geospatial software — delivered, unfunded
plans.description: DELIVERED, and left here rather than deleted so that what was asked for can be compared with what came of it. The plan was a public suite of traps with hand-computable answers (undetected CRS mismatch, feet read as metres, an unset TIFF predictor producing plausible terrain), a runner, a two-number score, and a clean set so that refusing everything cannot score well. All of it exists as Argleton — a separate project under a separate organisation, because an evaluation living inside the thing it evaluates can be dismissed in one line — Apache-2.0, with published runs and an archived release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22206349. It was built with no funding at all, which is the only reason this entry is worth reading: the estimate was EUR 20000.

plans.name: An open specification for the provenance manifest — delivered, unfunded
plans.description: DELIVERED, on the same terms as the entry above. The plan was a standalone specification with a versioned JSON Schema, a conformance suite of manifests that must validate and must be rejected, and a reference emitter of about a hundred lines that does not import MapSmith. All of it is public at github.com/mapsmith-ai/manifest-spec, archived at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22205213, with the schema served at the canonical URL its own $id names. One thing the estimate did not anticipate and the work found: the schema and the validator are independent implementations, and a generative conformance test derived from the schema showed they disagreed on 17 mutations out of 35 — which is the argument for why a specification needs a conformance suite rather than a document. The estimate was EUR 15000.

plans.name: Ongoing maintenance
plans.description: Security fixes, engine upgrades, and keeping the published benchmark honest — including republishing results that contradict earlier conclusions, which has already happened once.
